sub_units.name: Why Joins are needed
sub_units.content: In relational databases, data is distributed across multiple tables to avoid redundancy and maintain integrity. Joins are necessary to retrieve and combine this related data from two or more tables based on a logical relationship between them, allowing for comprehensive querying and analysis.

sub_units.name: INNER JOIN
sub_units.content: An INNER JOIN returns only the rows that have matching values in both tables being joined. If there is no match for a row in the specified columns, that row is excluded from the result set. It is the most common type of join used.

sub_units.name: LEFT JOIN
sub_units.content: A LEFT JOIN (or LEFT OUTER JOIN) returns all records from the left table, and the matched records from the right table. The result is NULL from the right side if there is no match. It is useful when you want to keep all primary records regardless of related secondary data.

sub_units.name: RIGHT JOIN
sub_units.content: A RIGHT JOIN (or RIGHT OUTER JOIN) returns all records from the right table, and the matched records from the left table. The result is NULL from the left side when there is no match. It is essentially the reverse of a LEFT JOIN.

sub_units.name: FULL JOIN
sub_units.content: A FULL JOIN (or FULL OUTER JOIN) returns all records when there is a match in either the left or right table records. Unmatched rows will contain NULL values for columns from the table that lacks a match. It combines the results of both LEFT and RIGHT joins.

sub_units.name: CROSS JOIN
sub_units.content: A CROSS JOIN returns the Cartesian product of the two tables, meaning it joins every row from the first table with every row from the second table. This join does not require a condition and can result in a very large dataset if the tables are large.

sub_units.name: SELF JOIN
sub_units.content: A SELF JOIN is a regular join, but the table is joined with itself. It is useful for querying hierarchical data or comparing rows within the same table. To perform a self join, you must use table aliases to distinguish the instances of the table.

sub_units.name: Joining multiple tables
sub_units.content: SQL allows joining more than two tables in a single query by chaining multiple JOIN clauses. Each JOIN typically connects a new table to the existing result set based on a specified relationship. Proper indexing and understanding of table relationships are crucial for performance.
